scenario.figure_or_table: Fig. 9 (with Table VI on PDF page 9): baseline chip, Splash2 fft, steady-state heat maps
scenario.description: Baseline 3D chip evaluated with Cool-3D (gem5 + McPAT/CACTI-3DD + HotSpot 7.0) running Splash2 fft. Steady-state heat maps are shown for the core layer and two memory layers. Reported maximum temperatures are 395.52 K (bottom core layer), 392.83 K (middle memory layer) and 390.57 K (top memory layer).
scenario.architecture: 3-layer stacked 3DIC: bottom layer 4 out-of-order 8-issue cores at 2 GHz (2x2) with 4KB/8KB 2-way L1 I/D caches and a shared 2MB L2; middle layer memory banks 0-15 (4x4); top layer memory banks 16-31 (4x4); 8GB memory with 32 banks and 8 banks per rank
scenario.workload: Splash2 fft benchmark, default problem size
scenario.operating_point: Steady-state HotSpot 7.0 simulation; passive heat sink with no microfluidic cooling; maximum temperature of the stack is the key metric

original_setup.solver: HotSpot 7.0 steady-state thermal simulation of a 3-layer 3D stack, with power inputs from McPAT (cores and caches) and a CACTI-3DD-based memory power calculator, and performance statistics from gem5 (PDF pages 3-6, 9-10)
original_setup.optimizer: None. Cool-3D is a manual what-if design space exploration framework. Stacking order, cooling pattern and L2 size are changed by hand across case studies, and RL-based optimization is listed only as future work (PDF pages 7-13).
original_setup.controller: None. No dynamic thermal management or runtime controller is used. The baseline is a steady-state run with a passive heat sink and no microfluidic cooling (PDF pages 9-10).
original_setup.benchmark: Splash2 fft at default problem size on the baseline 3-layer chip: bottom layer 4 cores (2x2, 2 GHz, out-of-order, 8-issue), middle layer memory banks 0-15, top layer memory banks 16-31, 4KB/8KB 2-way L1 I/D caches, 2MB shared L2, 8GB memory with 32 banks (Table VI, PDF page 9; Fig. 9, PDF page 10)

thermal_observable.location: Bottom core layer (cores 0-3) of the baseline chip, Splash2 fft heat map, Fig. 9. The same figure reports 392.83 K for the middle memory layer and 390.57 K for the top memory layer.
thermal_observable.aggregation: Maximum temperature on the layer from the steady-state HotSpot 7.0 heat map. The paper uses the maximum over the entire 3D stack as the key comparison metric.

physical_mismatches.reason: Block geometry and power are missing. The paper gives no block x, y, width or height in metres and no per-block watts for the baseline fft scenario. Fig. 9 shows only a temperature heat map with block labels and a colourbar, so no complete floorplan and power table can be built without inventing values. No pinned assets were supplied (assets list is empty) and the GitHub repository is described as still being released.

The scenario is a 3-layer core-plus-memory 3D stack with a passive heat sink. A 2.5D chiplet placement on an interposer (RLPlanner Ascend910 or ATPlace2.5D) cannot reproduce it, so 3D inter-layer coupling and vertical heat flow are mismatched.

Cooling mismatch. The baseline uses a passive heat sink with no microfluidic cooling, but the paper's main contribution is microfluidic cooling with vertical and 90-degree bent channel patterns in case studies 2a/2b. The baseline observable does not represent those cases.

Solver and power-model mismatch. The paper's power comes from gem5 + McPAT + CACTI-3DD, with per-benchmark and per-unit microarchitectural activity, and temperatures from HotSpot 7.0. A Studio solver with its own package and materials will not reproduce 395.52 K. The paper does not publish the HotSpot material, package or heat-sink parameters needed for calibration.

No optimizer, controller, transient behaviour or reliability analysis is in the baseline scenario. The run is steady-state only, and the paper has no power time series, so transient or controller comparison is not possible.

The text-layer values (395.52, 392.83 and 390.57) are consistent with the extraction. The colourbar on the Fig. 9 text layer ends near 394 K while the core-layer maximum is 395.52 K, and this was not examined visually. The decisive figure is therefore not visually verified.

These entries refer to 'RLPlanner Ascend910', 'ATPlace2.5D' and a 'Studio solver'. None of these appear in the paper or the supplied packet, so they are unsupported by the evidence. The 3D-stack-versus-2D mismatch itself is supported by Table VI.

The Hardik44 URL contains a space ('Gem5toMcPat parser') from pdftotext line breaking and underscore loss, so the URL is garbled and unverified. The same applies to the Splash2 URL, which was split across a line break in the source text. These resources are not paper inputs.
The 5.87x figure is described as 'on average' and the text does not tie it explicitly to fft only. It is a qualitative explanation and cannot be used to derive per-block power.

The steady-state claim is supported for the Fig. 9 baseline. The paper's headline novelty is microfluidic cooling (cases 2a/2b) plus the 3D stack and HotSpot 7.0, and none of this is reproducible as a plain 2D steady-state block-power problem. A 2D reproduction claim would be contradicted by the 3-layer stack with inter-layer coupling.

assessment.summary: The 2D screening label is not_2d_applicable and Studio did not run (simulation status skipped; simulation_allowed false). The scenario is the Cool-3D baseline Splash2 fft steady-state run on a 3-layer stack (4 cores, 2 MB shared L2, 32 memory banks, passive heat sink). The paper's printed layer maxima are 395.52 K (core layer), 392.83 K (middle memory layer) and 390.57 K (top memory layer). The proposed experiment kind is custom_2d_steady, but it has no floorplan blocks and no power_w, so the input gate fails (a custom experiment needs 1-128 blocks and a power_w object). Since it is a steady run, there is no transient trace. No bundled EV6/GCC adaptation and no pinned Ascend910 or ATPlace2.5D inputs were used, so no source commit or generated-placement assumption applies, and no illustrative input.flp or one-row input.ptrace was produced. Because the gate is closed, comparison_valid is false and no numerical comparison to 395.52 K, 392.83 K or 390.57 K is made. Qualitatively, the paper attributes the core0 hotspot to higher instruction counts (about 5.87x the other cores on average) and shows the core layer hotter than the memory layers. This cannot be checked against any Studio output. The mismatches are: (1) the paper is a 3D stack with vertical inter-layer coupling, while Studio is 2D/2.5D; (2) block geometry and per-block power are not published; (3) HotSpot 7.0 package, material and heat-sink parameters are not published, and the power model (gem5/McPAT/CACTI-3DD) differs from Studio's; (4) the baseline is passive-cooled, unlike the paper's microfluidic cases; (5) no transient or controller data exist. No exact replication is claimed.
